bull_bear.body:
- Market leadership in core categories - #1 in Fans and #1 in Residential Pumps, plus #3 in Storage Water Heaters, #3 in lighting (B2C) and #6 in Air Coolers, per external research reports and management estimates
- World's number one ceiling fan brand claim converted into an end-to-end on-pack campaign spanning print, retail visibility and packaging, reinforcing consumer trust
- 85+ year legacy with strong brand trust built through consistent quality and wide price-point coverage
- Zero debt and net cash positive status providing resilience and financial flexibility, with over 1,100 Crore of free cash at Group level
- Extensive multi-channel distribution - 2,76,000+ retailers, 7,000+ channel partners, 1,300+ authorised service centres and 7,000+ dealers and distributors (including Butterfly)
- Platform-first innovation strategy with an annual allocation of up to 100 Crore, plus rapid scaling of high-efficiency BLDC motor technology (e.g., SilentPro) across the fan portfolio
- Consumer-insight-led design contributing to lower product return rates and high satisfaction
- Supply chain and inventory optimisation improving service reliability
- Butterfly holds #1 brand position in LPG stainless steel gas stoves (PAN India) and #2 in LPG gas stoves, mixer grinders (South) and outer-lid pressure cookers
- Lighting segment achieving industry-leading margins by shifting from commoditised categories to premium consumer lighting and high-value B2B projects
- Early leadership in adjacent energy categories - market leadership in solar pumps and early presence in residential rooftop solar
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Regulatory and legal compliance — The BRSR identifies a complex and evolving regulatory environment across product, labour, environmental and corporate laws, which makes compliance critical for business continuity. Non-compliance would carry negative impact through penalties, litigation and operational disruption; mitigation is continuous monitoring of regulatory changes, internal audits, compliance training and strengthening governance frameworks.
- Regulatory energy-efficiency norms — Management lists regulatory energy efficiency norms among the key focus areas it tracks and mitigates. The portfolio is directly exposed to BEE star-rating and efficiency standard changes across fans, water heaters and pumps, which force re-engineering, re-rating and channel inventory transitions.
- Product quality, safety and sustainable product innovation — Compliance with product standards and growing demand for safe, innovative and sustainable products directly impact competitiveness; recalls or penalties carry negative impact while differentiation carries upside. Mitigation runs through strict quality controls, product testing, certifications and R&D investment in sustainable designs, supported by a stage-gate NPD framework, SAP Quality Module digitisation and QC Story projects.
- Brand reputation, customer trust and service quality — Brand perception and customer trust are influenced by product quality, service experience, digital feedback and counterfeit risks. The exposure is visible in service load - the new CRM platform temporarily impacted daily call registration inflow and March 2026 saw a 51% increase in average daily call registrations versus the previous period, which increased open calls. Mitigation is stronger product quality and service standards, grievance redressal, brand monitoring and anti-counterfeit measures.
- IT security, data protection and cybersecurity — Increased digitalisation exposes the Company to cyber threats, data breaches and misuse of confidential information, with negative impact from business disruption, data loss and remediation costs. Mitigation is robust IT security systems, access controls, cybersecurity audits, employee awareness and incident response plans.
- Supply chain resilience and sustainability — Dependence on suppliers and ESG non-compliance in the supply base may disrupt production and damage reputation; mitigation is supplier diversification and ESG due diligence. Operationally the Company flags stock-out and excess-inventory risk, addressed through standardised SOPs, rigorous vendor onboarding, Butterfly warehouse integration, Project ForeSight forecast enrichment and QR-code Track-and-Trace across all product lines and 30 warehouses.
- Business ethics and anti-corruption — Unethical business practices can lead to reputational damage, legal consequences and loss of stakeholder trust. Mitigation is a strong code of conduct, whistle-blower mechanism, employee awareness and periodic internal reviews.
- Workforce attrition and talent retention — Permanent employee turnover was 28.60% in FY 2025-26 versus 26.36% in FY 2024-25, and permanent worker turnover rose to 50.21% from 4.00%, driven by 163 workers opting for a Voluntary Retirement scheme in September 2025. Sustained high churn raises the execution risk on capability-building programmes (CLDP, FLDP, ELDP, Grow with Crompton) and on field/channel continuity.

business.body: Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals designs, manufactures and sells consumer electricals across fans, pumps, lighting and appliances, serving households, farmers and institutions through an extensive multi-channel PAN-India network of retailers, channel partners, dealers and authorised service centres. The portfolio spans Electrical Consumer Durables (fans, residential/agricultural/solar pumps, water heaters, air coolers, small domestic appliances and large kitchen appliances), B2C and B2B Lighting, the Butterfly kitchen-appliance business, and New Businesses covering solar rooftop solutions and wires and cables. Through its 'Crompton 2.0' transformation the Company is advancing consumer-centric innovation, portfolio premiumisation and stronger go-to-market capability while building new growth engines in integrated solar solutions and wires and cables.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Electrical Consumer Durables (ECD):** Fans - ceiling, pedestal, table, wall-mounted and exhaust fans, SilentPro BLDC fan platform, Pumps - residential, agricultural and solar pumps, Dura series upgrades for V3 and V4 submersibles, Aquagold, Flomax Dura, SWJ and monoblock / open well pumps, Smart controllers and MNRE-compliant solar pump solutions, Water heaters - in-house designed Solarium Blaze, Immersion Rods, Made-in-India Oil-Filled Radiators, Air coolers, Small domestic appliances - irons, mixer grinders, juicers, blenders and induction cooktops, Large kitchen appliances - chimneys and related kitchen solutions, India's first AQI-based chimney, Flame Pro Cooktop
- **Lighting:** B2C lighting - ceiling lights, lamps, battens, street lights, flood lights and accessories, B2B lighting - street, flood, industrial, professional and infrastructure lighting
- **Butterfly:** Mixer grinders, Pressure cookers, Gas stoves, Chimneys, Hobs, Cookware and other kitchen appliances, 'Idea First' innovation-led premium series, Alternate cooking appliances
- **New Businesses:** Solar rooftop solutions (ECD), Wires and cables (Lighting), Crompton Armor Wires

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Crompton 2.0: evolve the Company from a manufacturer with strong individual category positions into a diversified electrical consumer solutions platform serving the full spectrum of modern household needs
- Five pillars of the Crompton 2.0 roadmap - consumer-led innovation, portfolio premiumisation, go-to-market excellence, supply chain efficiency and digital enablement
- Disciplined expansion into adjacent categories rather than diversification for its own sake: wires and cables to extend presence across the complete electrical infrastructure of the home
- Build a credible and scalable solar platform - solar pumps leveraging established water-management and pump-engineering capabilities, and rooftop solar extending participation into distributed residential energy
- Strengthen leadership in core categories (fans, pumps, water heaters, air coolers and lighting) while further integrating Crompton's offerings within the Indian household's electrical ecosystem
- Engineering as the competitive edge - deepen institutional expertise in BLDC motor technology, pump engineering and energy-efficient product design, supported by R&D, manufacturing capability, in-house validation and talent development
- Deploy a zero-debt balance sheet so investment decisions can be guided purely by competitive logic and long-term growth priorities
- Embed sustainability directly into product innovation - BLDC fans, LED lighting, energy-efficient water heaters and solar pumps - to drive energy efficiency at scale while strengthening long-term portfolio relevance
- Align leadership incentives with long-term value creation through a long-term incentive programme linking the rewards of approximately 115 senior leaders to strategic and financial milestones
- Culture as an enabler: CREATE values (Care, Responsibility, Entrepreneurship, Accountability, Teamwork and Ethics) brought to life through the 'Fun Place to Work' framework, structured engagement surveys and regular townhalls
- The routed governance sections express capital-allocation intent as policy rather than as figures. The Board is responsible for developing strategy, overseeing material acquisitions and divestments, managing capital expenditure and the Company's capital structure, and handling other financing matters, and it oversees significant capital expenditures, acquisitions, mergers and other strategic initiatives essential to long-term success. It describes its primary role as trustee of shareholders' capital and commits to enhancing shareholder value while safeguarding the interests of all stakeholders. The Dividend Distribution Policy, framed because the Company is among the top 1,000 listed entities by market capitalisation under Regulation 43(A) of the SEBI Listing Regulations, states that dividend policy 'aims to strike a balance between the dual objectives of rewarding shareholders through Dividends and ploughing back earnings to support sustained growth' - rewarding shareholders by sharing a portion of profits while ensuring sufficient funds are retained for future growth, with the Company endeavouring to maintain a consistent approach to dividend pay-out plans. CSR spending follows a framework based on 'Responsible Business' and 'Shared Value' principles aligned to Schedule VII of the Companies Act. No payout ratio, buyback, leverage target or quantified capital-allocation target is stated in these sections.
- Environmental sustainability framework built on three areas - products, infra facilities and the supply chain - to reduce lifecycle impact, improve facility resource efficiency and strengthen value-chain sustainability performance
- Product-side priorities: development of BEE star-rated fans and water heaters, solar pump systems, product carbon footprint assessments and GreenPro-aligned development
- Facility-side priorities: energy conservation, renewable energy adoption, water stewardship and waste reduction
- Maintained the zero waste to landfill commitment, with continued recycling and reuse initiatives across operations
- Strengthened environmental monitoring through regular tracking of air, water and noise parameters
- Centralised ESG management software and an environmental performance dashboard supporting systematic, audit-ready tracking of energy, water, waste and emissions across the value chain
- Zero non-conformities in ISO surveillance audits
- BRSR assured by M/s. TUV India Private Limited - reasonable assurance for core indicators and limited assurance for non-core indicators; reporting boundary is standalone, with material subsidiary Butterfly Gandhimathi Appliances Limited reported for Principle 6
- Innovation ecosystem investment in advanced laboratories and testing capabilities including NVH testing, RoHS compliance, packaging performance testing and EMI/EMC validation
- Board and leadership diversity: women comprise 28.57% of the Board of Directors and 33.33% of Key Managerial Personnel
- SAKSHAM - Empowering Women at the Workplace, a structured upskilling programme for women employees
- Employee well-being and safety programmes: the 'Happy to Help' assistance programme, women's safety workshops, the SpeakUp platform and HRBP-led focus on openness, psychological safety and belonging
- Capability-building architecture for people development - CLDP for senior leaders, FLDP for mid-management, ELDP for Area Sales Managers, Grow with Crompton for Territory Sales Managers and a Belt Certification Model for structured sales capability progression
- Grievance redressal mechanisms in place for every stakeholder group - communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers (Vigil Mechanism and Whistleblower Policy), customers and value chain partners - with nil complaints pending for all groups other than customers
- Enterprise Risk Management governance spanning the Board Risk Management Committee, the Audit Committee, the Enterprise Risk Management Committee (bi-annual risk reviews) and the Risk Council
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The sections routed into this capex/expansion bundle contain NO company-specific capex or capacity-expansion disclosure for Crompton: no named plant, production line, brownfield/greenfield project, capacity addition, commissioning or ramp timeline, and no capex outlay or capital-work-in-progress commentary appears anywhere in the provided text. The Board's Report explicitly states the opposite of a pending project pipeline - 'No material changes or commitments have occurred between the end of the Financial Year and the date of this Report, which affect the Financial Statements' - and the only company-level operating development it records is that 'your Company's export business experienced growth' during the year. What the bundle does contain is three other things. First, the Management Discussion and Analysis INDUSTRY sections, which are third-party market-sizing and policy context rather than Crompton's own plans: fans (BLDC as the fastest-growing sub-segment, BLDC models consuming up to 50-65% less energy, and a highly localised, mature domestic induction-fan supply chain that supports cost competitiveness and reduces import dependence); pumps (agriculture, residential water management, construction and retail replacement demand); lighting (industry estimated at ~$4.9 billion in 2026 rising to ~$6.9 billion by 2031 at a ~7.2% CAGR, per Mordor Intelligence); small domestic appliances and large kitchen appliances (large cooking appliances valued at $2.37 billion in 2025 and projected to reach $7.23 billion by 2035 at an 11.8% CAGR); wires and cables (~$21 billion in 2025 to ~$35.6 billion by 2031 at a ~9% CAGR, with the organised segment now ~70% of housing wires and premiumisation toward FR, FRLS, heat-resistant and fire-survival variants); and solar (cumulative Indian solar capacity crossing ~100 GW in early 2025 against a 500 GW non-fossil target by 2030, rooftop solar at ~13.7 GW in 2024 projected to ~167 GW by 2034 with near-term estimates of 25-30 GW by FY27, PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana targeting 1 crore households with central financial assistance of up to 78,000 per household and the Rooftop Solar Programme Phase II extended through 2026, and PM-KUSUM targeting ~35 lakh solar pumps). These describe the addressable markets, not Crompton's build-out. Second, the Board's Report financial-performance, dividend, share-capital and liquidity sections, whose only expansion-relevant content is balance-sheet capacity to invest: the Company is debt-free as on March 31, 2026 and 'has maintained sufficient cash to meet its strategic and operational requirements', with credit ratings from CRISIL Ratings Limited and India Ratings and Research Private Limited. Third, the Notice of the 12th Annual General Meeting (adoption of accounts, declaration of dividend, re-appointment of Mr. Promeet Ghosh as a Director liable to retire by rotation, re-appointment of M S K A & Associates LLP as Statutory Auditors for a second five-year term to the conclusion of the Seventeenth AGM, and ratification of Cost Auditor remuneration for FY ending March 31, 2027). In short, the routed capex source for this company is industry-TAM and AGM-notice material plus the Board's Report; Crompton's own project, plant and capacity narrative is not present here, and the forward, checkable items available in this bundle are capital-allocation ones only.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The next phase of industry growth will be defined not by access but by aspiration - electrification has reached near-universal levels, and households in smaller towns and rural markets are now upgrading, replacing and premiumising, a demand profile that favours companies with strong engineering, deep distribution and trusted brands
- BEE standards are accelerating adoption of advanced technologies including BLDC motors and high-efficiency product architectures, and are simultaneously driving consolidation of market share from unorganised players toward established organised brands
- India's fast-moving electrical goods sector is estimated to exceed 1 Lakh Crore, and Crompton is positioned to capture a meaningful share of that growth
- Appliance penetration in India remains well below levels seen in comparable economies while technology transitions in fans, water management and energy infrastructure are still at an early stage - a widening gap between consumer expectations and current penetration
- Solar is a structural opportunity: PM-KUSUM is accelerating solar-powered irrigation adoption, creating a solar pumps market estimated at 30,000-35,000 Crore, while PM Surya Ghar is driving residential rooftop solar adoption at commercially meaningful scale
- Fans: the Indian electric fan market reached $2 billion in 2024 and is projected to grow to $5.64 billion by 2033 at a 12.2% CAGR, with a clear premiumisation shift toward decorative, silent, remote-controlled and IoT-enabled variants; BLDC fans consume up to 50-65% less energy than conventional models
- Pumps: demand anchored in residential water management, agriculture, construction and retail replacement, with long-term support from solar pump adoption under PM-KUSUM and a gradual shift to smart, IoT-enabled and solar-compatible pumps
- Water heaters and air coolers: low penetration, climate-linked demand, compact urban living and rising preference for smart, safe and energy-efficient appliances, with product innovation, distribution reach, after-sales service and brand trust as key differentiators
- Lighting: supported by LED replacement demand, infrastructure upgrades and public energy-efficiency programmes (UJALA, SLNP); industry estimated at ~$4.9 billion in 2026 rising to ~$6.9 billion by 2031 at a ~7.2% CAGR, with smart/connected lighting and B2B project lighting growing faster than the market
- Wires gaining from housing, renovation, safety awareness and the shift toward organised branded products
- Channel mix evolving: general trade continues to dominate on dealer trust, electrician influence and Tier II/III and rural reach, while modern trade, e-commerce and assisted digital discovery expand access to premium and new-age categories
- Localisation is a structural advantage - unlike several consumer durable categories, the induction fan segment benefits from a highly localised and mature domestic supply chain, supporting cost competitiveness and reducing import dependence
- Near-term performance may continue to be influenced by commodity-price volatility, weather-linked seasonality and uneven discretionary demand; near-term lighting demand may be affected by commodity volatility, channel destocking and pricing pressure in commoditised LED categories
- Macro backdrop supportive: India's GDP grew by 7.6% in FY26 and is projected to expand at 6.8% to 7.2% in FY27, with consumption sentiment aided by income tax relief and selective GST rationalisation, rural demand expected to recover and urban consumption to benefit from wage growth and premiumisation
- Medium-term industry outlook remains constructive, supported by India's expanding consumption base, home improvement trends, energy-efficiency awareness and demand for safer, smarter and more durable consumer electrical products
- Residential rooftop solar: early milestones include a robust order pipeline and active participation in government-led programmes, demonstrating that the Company is building competitive relevance quickly in this market
